title: Mark (25 April)
hook: the evangelist behind the Gospel that starts with a voice in the desert; his symbol is the lion

segments.voice: Yesterday, George, the soldier behind the dragon legend, whose real fight was a refusal. Your line was slay the dragon.

No manger. No angels. No family tree. One sentence of title, and then a shout from the wilderness. That's how the Gospel of Mark begins, in the Douay-Rheims: "The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God." A few lines later, a voice crying in the desert, John the Baptist in camel's hair, and Jesus already walking down to the river. Some readers call it the Gospel in a hurry. So who was its writer, and why is his sign a lion?
screen: `NO MANGER, NO ANGELS.` → `A SHOUT FROM THE WILDERNESS.` → `THE GOSPEL IN A HURRY.`

segments.voice: The Gospel itself never says who Mark was. Tradition fills in the name. An early bishop, Papias, wrote that Mark had been Peter's interpreter, and set down what Peter remembered of the Lord's words and deeds. Tradition also links him with the John Mark of the Acts of the Apostles, whose mother's house in Jerusalem was a place where the believers gathered, and who set out with Paul and Barnabas, then turned back partway. Paul refused to take him on the next journey, and Paul and Barnabas split over it. Yet in a later letter Paul asks for Mark to be brought to him, because he is useful. A young man who failed once, and was trusted again. Some readers even wonder whether the young man in Mark's Gospel who runs off naked from Gethsemane when Jesus is arrested is the writer quietly signing his work. Nobody can know. Now the lion. Christians long ago matched the four Gospel writers with the four living creatures in Ezekiel and Revelation: a man, a lion, an ox and an eagle. Saint Jerome gave Mark the lion, because his Gospel opens with a voice roaring in the wilderness: "A voice of one crying in the desert: Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make straight his paths." Venice later took Mark as its patron, and his winged lion still stands over the city. A short Gospel, a loud beginning, and a writer who was given a second chance.
screen: `THE GOSPEL NEVER NAMES ITS WRITER.` · `PETER'S INTERPRETER, TRADITION SAYS.` · `JOHN MARK: FAILED ONCE, TRUSTED AGAIN.` · `A LION FOR A ROARING VOICE.` · then, large: `PREPARE YE THE WAY OF THE LORD.`

segments.voice: Open a Bible or an app to Mark, chapter one, a short read, or just picture how it opens, with a voice in the desert. Notice the pace: Jesus is always on the move, the river, the desert, the lake, a house full of people, a lonely place before dawn. If you pray, ask to hear it as if for the first time; if you don't, simply take it as a story.
Mark. The evangelist the Church names as writer of the Gospel that opens with a voice in the desert, marked by the lion.
Your line: the lion. A writer who once turned back was trusted again. That's day nine hundred eighty-four.

howItsDone: Catholics keep the feast of Saint Mark the Evangelist on 25 April, reading from his Gospel at Mass; in Venice, where tradition says his relics rest, his day is a great civic and church feast.

chat.says: Why is Saint Mark always shown with a lion?
options: Jerome gave him the lion because his Gospel opens with a voice roaring in the wilderness.
Because Mark was thrown to the lions in Rome, and they refused to touch him.
Because Venice used a lion first, and the city later gave that sign to Mark.
chat.meaning: Christians matched the four evangelists with four living creatures; Jerome gave Mark the lion for the voice crying in the desert.
